title: Inverse systems satisfying finite-cover lifting define site points
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with finite limits. Let $(I,\geq,U_i,f_{ii'})$ be a directed inverse system of objects of $\mathcal C$: $I$ is a nonempty directed poset, each $i\geq i'$ has $f_{ii'}:U_i\to U_{i'}$, and $f_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $f_{i'i''}f_{ii'}=f_{ii''}$. Define $u(W)=\varinjlim_{i\in I}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(U_i,W)$. Assume that for every covering family $\{W_k\to W\}_{k\in K}$ and every $f\in u(W)$ there are $k\in K$ and $g\in u(W_k)$ whose image in $u(W)$ is $f$. Then $u$ commutes with finite limits and sends every covering family to a jointly surjective family. Consequently $u$ is a point of the site in the sense of Tag 00YC (Proposition proposition-point-limits), and the point-to-topos construction of Tag 00YA (Lemma lemma-point-site-topos) gives a geometric morphism $p:\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ [def-trf-geometric-morphism] whose inverse image satisfies the canonical identification $p^{-1}\mathcal F\cong\varinjlim_{i\in I}\mathcal F(U_i)$ for every sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$.

source.place: Tag 00YC (Proposition proposition-point-limits), together with Tag 00YA (Lemma lemma-point-site-topos); the finite-refinement passage is the final paragraph of Tag 00YQ (Proposition proposition-criterion-points).

proof.text: Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention] for all index sets and colimits. For any directed diagram of sets $(A_i)$, its colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] can be constructed from pairs $(i,a)$, $a\in A_i$, by the relation $(i,a)\sim(j,b)$ if their images agree at some $k\geq i,j$. This is an equivalence relation: symmetry and reflexivity are immediate, and transitivity follows by moving the two witnessing equalities to a common upper bound. A map out of this quotient is exactly a family of maps $A_i\to E$ compatible with transitions, proving its colimit universal property. Thus every colimit class has a representative, and equality is witnessed at a common later index. These observations apply to both $\operatorname{Hom}(U_i,W)$, with precomposition transitions, and $\mathcal F(U_i)$, with restriction transitions.

source.place: Tag 04AX (section-directed-colimits); the quotient construction and universal property of directed colimits of sets

proof.text:
For $h:W\to W'$, define $u(h)([i,a])=[i,h\circ a]$. Composition and identities follow on representatives, and postcomposition commutes with the precomposition transitions, so this is a functor. If $D$ is a finite diagram in $\mathcal C$, the limit universal property gives $\operatorname{Hom}(U_i,\lim D)\cong\lim_j\operatorname{Hom}(U_i,D_j)$, naturally in $i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits], taking the colimit over the nonempty directed poset $I$ gives
$$u(\lim D)\cong\varinjlim_i\lim_j\operatorname{Hom}(U_i,D_j)\cong\lim_j u(D_j).$$
These are the canonical comparison maps. Hence $u$ preserves finite limits, including the terminal object and all fibre products.

source.place: Tag 002W (lemma-directed-commutes); applied to the representable finite-limit comparison used in Sites Tag 00YC

proof.text:
For a sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$, put $S(\mathcal F)=\varinjlim_i\mathcal F(U_i)$, and for a sheaf morphism $a:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ put $S(a)([i,t])=[i,a_{U_i}(t)]$. Naturality of $a$ respects transitions, so $S$ is a functor. For a finite diagram $(\mathcal F_j)$, [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-finite-limits-objectwise], clauses (1) and (2), identify $(\lim_j\mathcal F_j)(U_i)$ with $\lim_j\mathcal F_j(U_i)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits] to obtain
$$S(\lim_j\mathcal F_j)\cong\varinjlim_i\lim_j\mathcal F_j(U_i)\cong\lim_j S(\mathcal F_j).$$
Thus $S$ preserves finite limits.

For a covering $\{W_k\to W\}_{k\in K}$, the stated hypothesis says that each $x\in u(W)$ is the image of some $y\in u(W_k)$. This is precisely joint surjectivity, and the maps are those given by postcomposition in Step 2. If the covering is empty, the hypothesis forces $u(W)=\varnothing$, so it also gives the required empty jointly surjective family. Step 2 additionally gives the pullback bijections $u(W_k\times_W V)\cong u(W_k)\times_{u(W)}u(V)$ for every $V\to W$.

source.place: Tag 00YC (proposition-point-limits), conditions (1) and (2), and Tag 00Y5 (definition-point), conditions (1) and (2)

proof.text:
Define the neighbourhood category $\mathcal N_u$ to have objects $(W,x)$ with $x\in u(W)$ and arrows $h:(V,y)\to(W,x)$ with $u(h)(y)=x$. Its stalk colimit $T(\mathcal F)=\varinjlim_{\mathcal N_u^{\mathrm{op}}}\mathcal F(W)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] consists of triples $(W,x,t)$ with relations $(W,x,t)\sim(V,y,\mathcal F(h)(t))$. Define
$$\alpha:T(\mathcal F)\to S(\mathcal F),\qquad [W,x,t]\mapsto[i,\mathcal F(a)(t)],\quad x=[i,a:U_i\to W].$$
If $a$ and $a'$ represent the same $x$, Step 1 gives a common $j$ with $a f_{ji}=a'f_{ji'}$; applying $\mathcal F$ makes the two output classes equal. For a pointed arrow $h:(V,y)\to(W,x)$, represent $y$ by $b:U_i\to V$; then $x=[i,hb]$ and $\mathcal F(b)\mathcal F(h)=\mathcal F(hb)$ verifies the stalk relation. In the other direction set $\beta([i,t])=[U_i,[i,\mathrm{id}_{U_i}],t]$. For $j\geq i$, the arrow $f_{ji}$ is pointed because $[j,f_{ji}]=[i,\mathrm{id}]$, so $\beta$ respects transitions. We have $\alpha\beta=1$; the pointed arrow $a:(U_i,[i,\mathrm{id}])\to(W,x)$ gives $\beta\alpha[W,x,t]=[W,x,t]$. Both formulas commute with sheaf morphisms. This proves the canonical natural isomorphism $T\cong S$ without a cofinality theorem.

source.place: The neighbourhood category and equation-stalk immediately before Tag 00Y5 (definition-point); explicit comparison for the inverse system in the proof of Tag 00YQ (proposition-criterion-points)

proof.text: The three clauses defining a site point (Tag 00Y5, definition-point) are now verified: joint surjectivity over coverings is Step 4; the covering pullback comparisons are bijections by Steps 2 and 4; and the associated stalk functor $T$ preserves finite limits by Steps 3 and 5. This is the point whose existence is expressed by Tag 00YC. We next construct its geometric morphism explicitly, rather than using a further point-construction lemma.

For a set $E$, put $R(E)(W)=\operatorname{Map}(u(W),E)$, with restriction along $h:V\to W$ given by precomposition with $u(h)$, and with a set map $E\to E'$ acting by postcomposition. We verify the sheaf equalizer condition [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Given compatible functions $q_k:u(W_k)\to E$ on a covering, choose, for $x\in u(W)$, a lift $y\in u(W_k)$ using Step 4 and assign $q(x)=q_k(y)$. If $y'\in u(W_l)$ is another lift, Step 2 lifts $(y,y')$ to $u(W_k\times_W W_l)$; compatibility of the functions there gives $q_k(y)=q_l(y')$. Thus the value is independent of the lift and defines a function whose restrictions are the $q_k$. It is unique by joint surjectivity. For an empty cover, $u(W)=\varnothing$ and there is exactly one function. Hence $R(E)$ is a sheaf, and $R$ is a functor $\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$.

source.place: Tag 00Y8 (lemma-point-pushforward-sheaf), proof of (1), with its sheaf gluing written out

proof.text:
A function $\phi:T(\mathcal F)\to E$ is, by the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], precisely a family $\phi_{W,x}:\mathcal F(W)\to E$ satisfying $\phi_{V,y}(\mathcal F(h)(t))=\phi_{W,x}(t)$ for each pointed arrow $h:(V,y)\to(W,x)$. Curry this family to $\tau_W(t)(x)=\phi_{W,x}(t)$. For any arrow $h:V\to W$ and $y\in u(V)$, the pointed arrow to $(W,u(h)y)$ makes that identity exactly
$$\tau_V(\mathcal F(h)t)(y)=\tau_W(t)(u(h)y),$$
which is naturality of $\tau:\mathcal F\to R(E)$. Evaluation at $x$ reverses currying, so these are inverse bijections. Precomposing a sheaf morphism changes $t$ by its section map in both formulas, and postcomposing $E\to E'$ changes their output in the same way. Thus they are natural in both variables and give $T\dashv R$, and Step 5 gives $S\dashv R$. With Step 3, this is a geometric-morphism datum [def-trf-geometric-morphism] from $\mathbf{Set}$ to $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$, with $p^{-1}=S$ and $p_*=R$. Its inverse image therefore has the claimed canonical formula $p^{-1}\mathcal F=\varinjlim_i\mathcal F(U_i)$. Since $T$ is the stalk and $R(E)(W)=\operatorname{Map}(u(W),E)$, this is exactly the point-to-topos construction of Tag 00YA(1).

source.place: Tags 00Y7 (lemma-adjoint-point-push-stalk), 00Y8 (lemma-point-pushforward-sheaf), and 00YA (lemma-point-site-topos), part (1); currying and its naturality written explicitly
